answer: Continuous co-presence attestation. Each identity must continuously solve a narrow physical challenge emitted by nearby peers, recorded on a shared knoll of timestamps that no single operator can backfill because the signals require distinct hardware clocks in distinct locations. An operator cloning identities pays for separate radios, power, and real estate per clone, so marginal cost stays physical rather than computational. Reputation peaks only at a verified zenith of sustained local presence, and any relic of stale attestation decays quickly.
